title: Mate preferences and the compatibility puzzle
title_zh: 配偶偏好与兼容性之谜
abstract: Researchers and laypeople commonly assume that romantic attraction depends, at least in part, on whether potential partners possess the traits that a person says they want. Yet recent studies suggest that such preference-matching effects (Preference × Trait statistical interactions) are often surprisingly small or even absent. Possible psychological explanations include (i) mate choice is multivariate, and so the matching effect for any given trait is heavily constrained, and (ii) traits permit flexible interpretations, in that the same trait can be interpreted differently depending on the partner to whom the trait belongs. Compatibility may derive not mainly from the matching of preferences and traits but rather from the way that two people recurrently extend and build upon shared positive experiences over time.
abstract_zh: 研究人员和普通大众普遍认为，浪漫吸引至少部分取决于潜在伴侣是否具备一个人声称想要的特质。然而，最近的研究表明，此类偏好匹配效应（Preference × Trait 统计交互作用）往往出奇地小，甚至完全缺失。可能的心理学解释包括：（i）配偶选择是多维的，因此任何单一特质的匹配效应都受到严重限制，以及（ii）特质允许灵活解释，即相同的特质在不同伴侣身上可能被不同地解读。兼容性可能主要源于两人随着时间的推移反复延伸并建立在共享的积极经验之上，而非主要源于偏好与特质的匹配。
